GLI is part of 5 of my public repositories, from 2014 to 2017.

What it was for: [Systems and infrastructure](@/projects/systems.md) (2), [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (2) and [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (1).

Most recently: [cluster](@/work/cluster.md): Run your own CoreOS/Kubernetes cluster; [csv2psql](@/work/csv2psql.md): Turns CSV into insert or update statements for PostgreSQL; [grache](@/work/grache.md): Cache for ruby gems.

2 of these projects run as live sites.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses GLI: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links GLI to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
